definitions.gloss: releasing fish or animals into the wild; stocking
definitions.explanation: The practice of releasing fish, fry, or other aquatic creatures into rivers, lakes, or the sea. Often done for conservation, fishing industry purposes, or as part of environmental restoration.
The controlled release of water from a dam or reservoir.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}に{稚魚|ちぎょ}を{放流|ほうりゅう}する。
examples.english: To release fry into the river.

examples.japanese: {毎年|まいとし}{春|はる}にサケの{放流|ほうりゅう}が{行|おこな}われる。
{地域|ちいき}の{子|こ}どもたちが{放流|ほうりゅう}{体験|たいけん}に{参加|さんか}した。
examples.english: Local children participated in a fish-release experience.

examples.japanese: ダムから{水|みず}を{放流|ほうりゅう}する。
examples.english: To discharge water from a dam.

examples.japanese: {大雨|おおあめ}のため、{緊急|きんきゅう}{放流|ほうりゅう}が{実施|じっし}された。
examples.english: Due to heavy rain, an emergency water discharge was carried out.

examples.japanese: ダムの{放流|ほうりゅう}により{下流|かりゅう}の{水位|すいい}が{上昇|じょうしょう}した。
examples.english: The water level downstream rose due to the dam discharge.

notes: For sense 1, commonly associated with conservation activities such as {稚魚|ちぎょ}の{放流|ほうりゅう} (releasing fry) and サケの{放流|ほうりゅう} (salmon stocking). For sense 2, {緊急|きんきゅう}{放流|ほうりゅう} (emergency discharge) is an important term seen in weather warnings during heavy rainfall.
